Night Trains Return to the Mountain Corridor

The first overnight passenger train in more than a decade left the valley station shortly after sunset on Friday, carrying commuters, students, and hikers toward towns that had lost late service during earlier budget cuts.

Transit planners restored the route after a year-long trial showed that evening buses were routinely full and that weekend visitors were driving to trailheads before dawn.

The new timetable uses existing track and refurbished sleeper cars, but stations along the corridor received lighting, platform, and accessibility upgrades before service resumed.

Officials will review ridership, reliability, and winter operating costs after six months. Local governments have committed bridge funding if ticket revenue takes longer than expected to stabilize.

Passengers on the inaugural trip said the practical benefit was simple: they could finish a full workday in the city and still reach smaller mountain communities without renting a car.
